channel.title: mvdmio blog
channel.description: Posts by Michiel van der Meer on agile, remote work and leading software teams.

item.title: Effective .NET Web development for individuals and small teams
item.description: Michiel on why server-side rendering with Hotwire brings Rails-style productivity to ASP.NET for small teams.

item.title: The water cooler is a silly place
item.description: Michiel argues the water cooler rarely solves real problems, and that focused, uninterrupted work matters more than office chatter.

item.title: Developers are not socially awkward introverts; here is how to understand us
item.description: Michiel explains the personality traits that make good programmers, and why headphones and quiet rooms aren't a social problem.

item.title: What it takes to lead software development teams effectively
item.description: Michiel on the milestones, expectations and uninterrupted time that effective software teams need from their leads.

item.title: You can only make a first impression as often as you want
item.description: Michiel on why showing an unfinished product to customers is validation, not a wasted first impression.

item.title: You can't do agile without a customer
item.description: Michiel on why agile only works when real end-users, not internal stakeholders, validate the product.

item.title: The unwritten rules of remote communication
item.description: Michiel's rules of thumb for when to call, message or email a remote colleague.

item.title: Agile bill of rights
item.description: Michiel records the Customer and Developer Bill of Rights from Robert C. Martin's Clean Agile.

item.title: Improving on the 'yearly disappointment' at work
item.description: Michiel on why performance reviews should stop deciding pay raises, and what to discuss instead.

item.title: List of fully-remote businesses
item.description: A sourced list of fully-remote businesses, from payroll platforms to online events tools.
